trap-closing-aphorism.evidence: The block ends on a quantitative bound rather than a flourish. Whether that bound is TRUE is a separate matter - it is not, as stated; see notes.
trap-closing-aphorism.notes: TWO CONTENT DEFECTS, both concrete. (1) *** THE CLOSING BOUND IS FALSE AS STATED. *** 'The self-deformation is small: $|\delta q / q_0| < 0.1\%$ for all nuclei.' Computing delta q = [C(Z,2)-C(N,2)]/A^2 . hbar_q^2 at q_0: the bound holds along the valley of stability (Fe-56 0.031%, Pb-208 0.093%, U-238 0.0999% - right at the edge) but FAILS for neutron-rich nuclides that exist and are produced: Mg-40 (Z=12, N=28) gives 0.172%, Ca-60 gives 0.145%, O-24 at the neutron drip line gives 0.141%, Sn-137 gives 0.119%. The correct scope is 'for nuclei near the valley of stability', and the true supremum of the formula is 0.44% (the pure-proton limit C(A,2)/A^2 -> 1/2). This matters because the sibling rem:hadron-q-self-correction-interpretation quotes a 0.1-0.4% range for a DIFFERENT quantity (the differential shift), so the two blocks' numbers are easy to conflate. (2) THE A^2 EXPONENT IS NOT WHAT THE STATED REASON GIVES: 'The $A^2$ normalization reflects linking density: crossings occupy a volume proportional to $A$, making the crossing density per unit volume $\ell_{\mathrm{net}}/A^2$.' A quantity divided by a volume proportional to A is proportional to $\ell_{\mathrm{net}}/A$, not $/A^2$. Either the volume scales as A^2, or the normalisation is by something other than volume (pair count C(A,2) ~ A^2/2 would give A^2 directly and is the likelier intent). As written the justification contradicts the exponent it justifies.
